claim.claim-text: CLAIMS:

1. A composition comprising a biologically effective amount of an anti-VEGF antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, that binds to substantially the same epitope as the monoclonal antibody ATCC PTA 1595 and that significantly inhibits VEGF binding to the VEGF receptor VEGFR2 (KDR/Flk-1) without significantly inhibiting VEGF binding to the VEGF receptor VEGFRl (Flt-1).
2. The composition of claim 1, wherein said antibody is a monoclonal antibody or an antigen-binding fragment thereof.
3. The composition of claim 1 or 2, wherein said antibody is an IgG antibody or an IgM antibody.
4. The composition of claim 1 or 2, wherein said antibody is an scFv, Fv, Fab', Fab, diabody, linear antibody or F(ab')2 antigen-binding fragment of an antibody.
5. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said antibody is a dimer, trimer or multimer of said antibody or antigen-binding fragments thereof.
6. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said antibody is a human, humanized or part-human antibody or antigen-binding fragment thereof.
7. The composition of claim 6, wherein said antibody comprises an antigen-binding region of said antibody operatively attached to a human antibody framework or constant region.
8. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said antibody is a chimeric antibody.
9. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said antibody is a recombinant antibody.

10. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said antibody comprises at least a first variable region that includes an amino acid sequence region having the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:7 or SEQ ID NO:9.
11. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said antibody is the monoclonal antibody ATCC PTA 1595.
12. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to at least a first biological agent.
13. The composition of claim 12, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to at least a first agent that cleaves a substantially inactive prodrug to release a substantially active drug.
14. The composition of claim 13, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to alkaline phosphatase that cleaves a substantially inactive phosphate-prodrug to release a substantially active drug.
- 15. The composition of claim 12, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to at least a first therapeutic or diagnostic agent.
16. The composition of claim 15, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to at least a first therapeutic agent.
17. The composition of claim 16, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to at least a first and a second therapeutic agent.

18. The composition of claim 16 or 17, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to at least a first chemotherapeutic agent, radiotherapeutic agent, anti-angiogenic agent, apoptosis- inducing agent, steroid, antimetabohte, anthracycline, vinca alkaloid, anti-tubulin drug, antibiotic, cytokine, alkylating agent or coagulant.

19. The composition of claim 18, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to a cytotoxic, cytostatic or anticellular agent capable of killing or suppressing the growth or cell division of endothelial cells.
20. The composition of claim 19, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to a plant-, fungus- or bacteria-derived toxin.

21. The composition of claim 20, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to an A chain toxin, a ribosome inactivating protein, α-sarcin, gelonin, aspergillin, restrictocin, a ribonuclease, an epipodophyllotoxin, diphtheria toxin or Pseudomonas exotoxin.
22. The composition of claim 21, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to ricin A chain or deglycosylated ricin A chain.
23. The composition of claim 18, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to an antiangiogenic agent.
24. The composition of claim 23, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to an angiopoietin.
25. The composition of claim 24, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to angiopoietin-2.
26. The composition of claim 23, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to angiostatin, vasculostatin, canstatin or maspin.
27. The composition of claim 23, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to endostatin.
28. The composition of claim 18, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to an anti- tubulin drug.

29. The composition of claim 28, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to an anti- tubulin drug selected from the group consisting of colchicine, taxol, vinblastine, vincristine, vindescine and a combretastatin.
30. The composition of claim 18, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to a coagulant.

31. The composition of claim 30, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to a coagulant selected from the group consisting of Factor Il/IIa, Factor VII/NIIa, Factor D /TXa, Factor X/Xa, a vitamin K-dependent coagulation factor that lacks the Gla modification,
Russell's viper venom Factor X activator, thromboxane A2, thromboxane A2 synthase and α2- antiplasmin.

32. The composition of claim 30, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to Tissue Factor, a human Tissue Factor, a mutant Tissue Factor deficient in the ability to activate Factor VII, truncated Tissue Factor or to a dimeric, trimeric or polymeric Tissue Factor or Tissue Factor derivative.
33. The composition of claim 32, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to truncated Tissue Factor.
34. The composition of claim 15, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to a diagnostic, imaging or detectable agent.
35. The composition of claim 34, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to an X-ray detectable compound, a radioactive ion or a nuclear magnetic spin-resonance isotope.
36. The composition of claim 34, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to biotin, avidin or to an enzyme that generates a colored product upon contact with a chromogenic substrate.

37. The composition of any one of claims 12 through 33, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to said biological agent as a fusion protein prepared by expressing a recombinant vector that comprises, in the same reading frame, a DNA segment encoding said antibody operatively linked to a DNA segment encoding said biological agent.
38. The composition of any one of claims 12 through 33, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to said biological agent via a biologically releasable bond or selectively cleavable linker.

39. The composition of claim 38, wherein said antibody is operatively attached to said biological agent via a peptide linker that includes a cleavage site for urokinase, pro-urokinase, plasmin, plasminogen, TGFβ, staphylokinase, Thrombin, Factor IXa, Factor Xa, a metalloproteinase, an interstitial collagenase, a gelatinase or a stromelysin.
40. The composition of any one of claims 12 through 36, wherein said antibody is directly attached to said biological agent.
41. The composition of any one of claims 15 through 36, wherein said antibody is attached to a second antibody, or antigen binding region thereof, that binds to said therapeutic or diagnostic agent.
42. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said composition is pharmaceutically acceptable.composition.
43. The composition of claim 42, wherein said pharmaceutically acceptable composition is formulated for parenteral or intravenous administration.
44. The composition of any preceding claim, wherein said composition further comprises a second therapeutic agent.
45. The composition of claim 44, wherein said second therapeutic agent is a second anti- cancer agent.

46. The composition of claim 45, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is a chemotherapeutic agent, radiotherapeutic agent, anti-angiogenic agent, apoptosis-inducing agent, anti-tubulin drug; or a prodrug or tumor-targeted version of a chemotherapeutic agent, radiotherapeutic agent, anti-angiogenic agent, apoptosis-inducing agent or anti-tubulin drug.
47. The composition of claim 46, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is an angiopoietin or a tumor-targeted angiopoietin .
48. The composition of claim 47, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is angiopoietin-2 or a tumor-targeted angiopoietin-2.
49. The composition of claim 46, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is endostatin or a tumor-targeted endostatin.
50. The composition of claim 46, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is an anti-tubulin drug or a tumor-targeted anti-tubulin drug.

51. The composition of claim 46, wherein said second anti-cancer agent is an antibody- therapeutic agent constmct comprising a therapeutic agent that is operatively linked to a second antibody, or antigen binding fragment thereof, that binds to a surface-expressed, surface-accessible or surface-localized component of a tumor cell, tumor vasculature or tumor stroma.
52. The composition of any preceding claim, for use in therapy.
53. The composition of any one of claims 1 through 11 or claims 34 through 36, for use in diagnosis.
54. The composition of any one of claims 1 through 11 or claims 23 through 27, for use in inhibiting angiogenesis upon administration to an animal.
55. The composition of any one of claims 12 through 41, for use in delivering a biological agent to a vascularized tumor upon administration to an animal with a vascularized tumor.
56. The composition of any preceding claim, for use in treating cancer.
57. Use of a composition in accordance with any preceding claim in therapy.
58. Use of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 11 or claims 23 through 27 in the manufacture of a medicament for treating a disease by inhibiting angiogenesis.
59. Use of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 12 through 41 in the manufacture of a medicament for treating cancer by delivering a biological agent to a vascularized tumor.
60. Use of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56 in the manufacture of a medicament for treating cancer.

61. A composition comprising a biologically effective amount of an anti-VEGF antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, that binds to substantially the same epitope as the monoclonal antibody 2C3 (ATCC PTA 1595) for use in inhibiting angiogenesis without substantial inhibition of macrophages, osteoclasts or chondroclasts.

62. Use of a composition comprising a biologically effective amount of an anti-VEGF antibody, or antigen-binding fragment thereof, that binds to substantially the same epitope as the monoclonal antibody 2C3 (ATCC PTA 1595) in the manufacture of a medicament for treating cancer by inhibiting VEGF binding to the VEGF receptor VEGFR2 (KDR/Flk-1) without significantly inhibiting VEGF binding to the VEGF receptor VEGFRl (Flt-1).
63. A kit comprising at least a first composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56.

64. A kit comprising at least a first composition in accordance with claim 13 or 14 and at least a second composition comprising a substantially inactive prodrug that is cleaved by the biological agent attached to the antibody in said first composition to release a substantially active drug.
65. A kit comprising at least a first composition in accordance with claim 14 and at least a second composition comprising combretastatin phosphate.
66. A hybridoma that produces a monoclonal antibody as defined in any one of claims 2 through 11.
67. Monoclonal antibody ATCC PTA 1595.

68. A method for preparing an anti-VEGF antibody that binds to substantially the same epitope as the monoclonal antibody ATCC PTA 1595, comprising immunizing a non-human animal with an immunizing composition comprising at least a first immunogenic VEGF component and selecting from the immunized animal an antibody that substantially cross- reacts with the monoclonal antibody ATCC PTA 1595.
69. The method of claim 68, wherein said non-human animal is a transgenic mouse that comprises a human antibody library.
70. The method of claim 68 or 69, comprising obtaining the nucleic acids that encode said anti-VEGF antibody and expressing said nucleic acids to obtain a recombinant anti-VEGF antibody.
71. The method of any one of claims 68 through 70, comprising:
(a) administering to a non-human animal an immunizing effective amount of a composition comprising at least a first immunogenic VEGF component;
(b) preparing a combinatorial immunoglobulin phagemid library expressing RNA isolated from the spleen of the immunized animal;
(c) selecting from the phagemid library a clone that expresses an anti-VEGF antibody that substantially cross-reacts with the monoclonal antibody 2C3 (ATCC PTA 1595); and
(d) expressing the anti-VEGF antibody-encoding nucleic acids from said selected clone to provide a recombinant anti-VEGF antibody.

72. A method of detecting VEGF, comprising contacting a composition suspected of containing VEGF with a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56, under
conditions effective to allow the formation of VEGF/antibody complexes and detecting the complexes so formed.

73. A method of inhibiting VEGF binding to the VEGF receptor VEGFR2, without significantly inhibiting VEGF binding to the VEGF receptor VEGFRl, comprising contacting a homogeneous or heterogeneous population of cells that express VEGFR2 (KDR/Flk-1) and VEGFRl (Flt-1) with a biologically effective amount of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56.

74. A method of specifically inhibiting VEGF-induced endothelial cell proliferation, comprising contacting a population of endothelial cells with a biologically effective amount of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56.

75. A method of inhibiting VEGF-induced endothelial cell proliferation, without significantly inhibiting VEGF-stimulated macrophage, osteoclast or chondroclast function, comprising contacting a tissue that contains endothelial cells and at least one of macrophages, osteoclasts and chondroclasts with a biologically effective amount of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56.

76. A method of inhibiting angiogenesis, comprising contacting a population of potentially angiogenic blood vessels with an anti-angiogenic composition comprising a biologically effective amount of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56.

77. A method of treating an angiogenic disease, comprising administering to an animal with an angiogenic disease at least a first pharmaceutical composition that comprises a therapeutically effective amount of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56.

78. A method for delivering a diagnostic or therapeutic agent to a vascularized tumor, comprising administering to an animal with a vascularized tumor a biologically effective amount of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 12 through 41.

79. A method for treating cancer, comprising administering at least a first pharmaceutical composition to an animal that has, or is at risk for developing, a vascularized solid tumor, a metastatic tumor or metastases from a primary tumor; wherein said at least a first pharmaceutical composition comprises a therapeutically effective amount of a composition in accordance with any one of claims 1 through 56.
80. The method of claims 78 or 79, further comprising subjecting said animal to radiotherapy.
81. A method for treating cancer, comprising:

(a) administering a first composition in accordance with claim 13 or 14 to an animal that has a vascularized solid tumor, a metastatic tumor or metastases from a primary tumor, thereby localizing the antibody of said composition to the tumor vasculature or stroma; and

(b) subsequently administering to said animal a second composition that comprises a substantially inactive prodrug that is cleaved by the biological agent attached to the antibody in said first composition, thereby releasing a substantially active drug specifically within said tumor vasculature or stroma.
82. The method of any one of claims 78 through 81, wherein said animal is a human patient.
